body:
## Triage and implementation notes (agent, read against `main` 575f02d8)

**Classification:** `enhancement` · `effort:high` (several crates, changes what every post reads, a refusal law - safety floor) · `area:post`, `area:ui`, `area:mcp`. The priority stays with the maintainer (`P?`); by AGENTS.md's MCP rule it would be `P1` once unpaused.

### The report checks out

- The table is `WCS_SLOTS` at `crates/app/src/operation/types/sel.rs:6`; the one law for the index is `setup::wcs_slot` (`crates/app/src/setup.rs:106`).
- `posting::wcs_context` (`crates/app/src/posting.rs:940`) hands the WORD to the post crate (`Dump::wcs: &str`, `crates/post/src/post/mod.rs:99`), which writes it as `PARAM WorkOffset` (`mod.rs:211`).
- All 11 shipped scripts read it as a word. Fanuc, Haas, Mazak and Doosan DNM parse it back with `slotOf` for the probe registers (`#5221 + 20 x slot`); Heidenhain regex-matches it (`heidenhain.cps:238`); Sinumerik has `frameOf` (`sinumerik.cps:536`); Carvera, Fanuc lathe, Tormach mill / lathe / plasma write it verbatim.
- The six-offset cap sits in core at `SetSetupWorkOffset::new` (`commands/setup_wcs.rs:35`), the loader (`project/wcs_migrate.rs:88`, `project/apply.rs:765`) and `setup::work_offset` (`setup.rs:96`).

### Things the proposal does not cover yet

1. **`WCS_SLOTS` is also a list of reserved entity names**, not only words: `commands/setup.rs:107,121`, `commands/setup_delete.rs:54`, `commands/tool.rs:24`, `project/validate.rs:88,90,291`, `project/wcs_one.rs`, `setup.rs:218,270`. With the legacy `G54` entity name out of scope, point 5 cannot remove the table from app: split it into a private legacy-name list (reservations and the migrations) and delete only the word uses.
2. **An index the post cannot express must block the post, never fall back.** `setup::work_offset` today reads an out-of-range stored index as "no pick", i.e. `G54`. Once the limit is the post's, a setup at offset 9 switched to a 6-offset post would silently post at offset 1 - a part cut at the wrong zero. The filter has to go; the post-time gate refuses by setup name, and the travel check (`wcs_context`) and the setup sheet (`setup_sheet/sections.rs:123`) must not fall back either.
3. **Posts are resolved per setup** (`posting_mounts::post_of_setup`, `setup_mount::post_of`), so names and the maximum come from the setup's own post, not the document's.
4. **The probe record already carries an index, 0-based:** `SetWorkOffset` is `0..=5`, `-1` for none (`crates/post/src/post/probe_rec.rs:153-192`), and the scripts write `P(n+1)`. `WorkOffset` 1-based beside it is a trap; either say so in `docs/CNC-INTERMEDIATE.md` or make both 1-based under the new flag. The probe arithmetic (`#5221 + 20 x slot`) only reaches offsets 1-6, so a probe that reads or sets an extended offset is refused by name until a dialect maps its registers.
5. **Sinumerik changes output for offsets 5 and 6.** The script writes the word verbatim in the section opener (`sinumerik.cps:351`), so today those post as `G58` / `G59`, while its own `frameOf` and probe message say the settable frames are `G54..G57` and `G505..G599`. An index mapping would write `G505` / `G506`. No golden covers it (the one Sinumerik golden among the 7 with `G55..G59`, `nc/synth_sinumerik.nc`, carries only `G55`), so "byte-identical" still holds, but it is a behaviour change to state in the changelog - and worth confirming against Siemens' public documentation as a bug of its own.
6. **Three scripts declare no mode flags today** (`carvera.cps`, `tormach.cps`; `tormach-plasma.cps` only `coolantModes`), so "every shipped script declares the flag" is new work there. The flag pattern to copy is `crates/post/src/post/js.rs:162-231`; the refusal pattern is `engine.rs:140-160`.
7. **Other word users:** `posting_wcs_slot::shared_word_problems` (two setups, one word, different zeros) should compare indexes; `posting_wcs_rotation.rs:111`, `setup_sheet/sections.rs:126`, `mcp/job.rs:52`, `mcp/setup_tools.rs:147-170`, and in the UI `setup_wcs_pick.rs`, `browser_tree.rs:208`, `heights_page.rs:114`, `interact.rs:614`, `state.rs:3288`.
8. **Older builds cannot open a file that uses offset 7 or higher** (their loader refuses it). No format version step is needed, but the release notes should say so.

### The open questions

- **Where the name lookup lives.** In the post crate: evaluate once at script load, next to the flag reads - a declared maximum (e.g. `workOffsetMax`) and the names for `1..=max` from `workOffsetName(n)` - and return a plain table. In app: one function (e.g. `setup::work_offset_names(world, setup)`) caches that table per resolved post and script text; `setup::wcs_label` and the setup sheet read it. The UI only calls app, so the layering holds and no script runs per frame. The table is display only - it must never feed the stream; `setup::wcs_slot` stays the single source of the index.
- **MCP input.** Accept `index` (1-based) and keep the words `G54`..`G59` as aliases for 1-6; return `index` and `name`, and keep `word` as an alias of `name` so existing callers do not break. The camcraft-mcp skill doc needs the change.
- **Per-post maximum.** Yes: the script declares it, the combo lists `1..=max` of the setup's post, and no post or an unflagged script means 6. Core keeps only a sanity bound (the height hash at `operation/params.rs:34` stores the index in a `u8`).
- **Does anything parse the word back?** The simulator does not (`crates/sim/src` has no reference). Test harnesses do: `crates/app/tests/macro_b/mod.rs` models the `G54..G59` registers and refuses `G10 L2 P>6`; `tormach_lathe_support/mod.rs` and 17 app test files mention `G55..G59`. 148 goldens contain a `G5x` word, 7 of them `G55..G59`. None changes while 1-6 map to the same words.

### Suggested slices (stacked, goldens byte-identical in each)

1. **Post crate and scripts.** The `workOffsetIndex` flag; the dump carries the index; a flagged script gets the number, an unflagged one the word for 1-6 and a refusal by setup name above 6; all 11 scripts map the index themselves and declare their maximum and names; docs. Tests in `crates/post/tests`, running the post engine on recorded toolpath files (the direction of #926): offsets 1, 6, 7, the dialect's maximum and one past it.
2. **App.** `wcs_context` returns the index; the cap moves from the command and loader to the post-time gate plus a command-time check against the setup's post; labels, setup sheet and refusal texts use the name table; the legacy entity-name list is split off.
3. **UI and MCP.** The combo from the table; MCP index and aliases; structural (AccessKit) assertions - no snapshot PNG changes.

Extended-offset words per dialect (Fanuc `G54.1 Pn`, Haas `G154 Pn` / `G110+`, LinuxCNC `G59.1`-`G59.3`, Sinumerik `G505+`, Heidenhain preset rows) are from general knowledge here: each needs checking against that control's public manual before it is written into a script.

**Wording:** #876 settled on plain English for this in the UI ("Work offset (G54-G59)"). "WCS n (name)" would read better as "Work offset 2 (G55)", and "Work offset 2" when the post gives no name.

Related since this was filed: #918 put a unit word in the opening blocks of five posts (no conflict, but the same lines); #902 is the same "one source, the post only writes it" rule for units; #926 / #923 decide where post-script tests live.

Maintainer decision (2026-11-11, through the orchestrator's question dialog): unpaused - `P?` swapped for `P1`. To be worked in the three stacked slices of the comment above, after #934 (the Sinumerik G58/G59 wrong output) is fixed.
